Ian Rickson more than revives Edward Albee’s 2002 masterpiece The Goat, at the Haymarket.
It’s nigh on two hours of break-free entrenched family warfare in a single setting, but thanks to stellar performances and Albee’s masterful rat a tat dialogue your attention never flags.
What starts as an uncomfortable black comedy slowly turns tragic, with the gay son of the house (Archie Madekwe) struggling to accept his perfect dad could do such things.

cn.t: Critics largely praise this Albee revival, with Damian Lewis and Sophie Okonedo earning strong notices for their performances. Some find the provocative material uneven, but most agree it's a bold, compelling production.
